**SECTION C: READING COMPREHENSION**

*Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Use complete English sentences in your answers.*

These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than clerks who work in offices. People who work in offices are frequently referred to as “white collar workers” for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work. Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white collar workers. This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs, who worked as a dustman for a Development Corporation.

When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job. He simply told her that he worked for the corporation. Every morning, he left home dressed in a fine black suit. He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman. Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit. Alf did this for two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret. Alf's wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job. He will soon be working in an office as a junior clerk. He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money. From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him “Mr. Bloggs”, not “Alf”.

*(Culled from University English for Francophone Africa, 2008)*

questions.enonce_markdown: **1)** Who are white collar workers and why are they given this name?
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Répondre à une question de compréhension suppose de retrouver d'abord, dans le texte, le passage précis qui contient l'information demandée, puis de la reformuler avec ses propres mots en phrase complète (sujet + verbe), sans se contenter de recopier la phrase du texte ni de répondre par un seul mot : la citation confirme la réponse, la reformulation prouve qu'elle est comprise.

Le texte définit ce groupe dès la première phrase : « People who work in offices are frequently referred to as “white collar workers” for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work. » La réponse doit nommer qui ils sont (des employés de bureau) et reformuler la raison du nom (le port habituel d'un col et d'une cravate au travail).

Réponse : **White collar workers are people who work in offices. They are given this name because they usually wear a collar and a tie to go to work, unlike people who do manual work.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **2)** What secret did Alf's fellow dustmen have to keep?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Le texte précise : « Alf did this for two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret. » Le secret en question est explicité plus haut : Alf cachait à sa femme qu'il travaillait comme éboueur (dustman), en lui faisant croire qu'il occupait un emploi de bureau.

Réponse : **Alf's fellow dustmen had to keep the secret that Alf actually worked as a dustman, and not in an office as he had made his wife believe.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **3)** What particular advantage does Alf expect to get from working as a junior clerk?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Le texte indique qu'Alf gagnera deux fois moins d'argent dans son nouvel emploi (« He will be earning only half as much as he used to »), mais qu'il juge que cette perte financière est largement compensée par un gain différent : « he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money. » L'avantage recherché n'est donc pas financier mais social.

Réponse : **Alf expects to gain a rise in social status - being seen as a “white collar worker” and called “Mr. Bloggs” instead of “Alf” - even though he will earn only half as much money as before.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **4)** Why did Alf not want to reveal the nature of his job to his wife?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Le texte le dit explicitement dès le deuxième paragraphe : « Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job. » Cette gêne s'explique par le statut peu valorisant du métier d'éboueur comparé à celui d'employé de bureau, valorisé socialement (voir le premier paragraphe sur les « white collar workers »).

Réponse : **Alf did not want to reveal his job to his wife because he was too embarrassed about being a dustman, a manual job that carries far less social status than an office job.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **5)** Why did his wife stay for 2 years without discovering the real profession of her husband?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Le texte détaille la stratégie quotidienne d'Alf : « Every morning, he left home dressed in a fine black suit. He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman... Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit. » À cela s'ajoute la complicité de ses collègues, qui gardaient le secret.

Réponse : **His wife did not discover the truth because Alf left home every morning dressed in a suit, changed into overalls once out of her sight, worked as a dustman all day, then showered and put his suit back on before coming home at night; in addition, his fellow dustmen kept his secret and never revealed it to her.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **6)** In your opinion, why do manual workers tend to receive more money than office clerks?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cette question d'opinion invite à prolonger l'idée du texte : les gens sont prêts à « sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white collar workers », c'est-à-dire qu'ils acceptent de gagner moins pour obtenir un emploi de bureau valorisant. Cela suggère une explication économique simple : un emploi convoité pour son prestige attire davantage de candidats, ce qui permet aux employeurs de payer moins ; à l'inverse, un travail manuel, souvent plus dur, plus salissant ou moins valorisé socialement, doit être mieux rémunéré pour attirer des travailleurs.

Réponse (avis argumenté, plusieurs formulations sont acceptables si elles sont justifiées) : **In my opinion, manual workers tend to receive more money than office clerks because manual work is often harder, dirtier or less socially valued, so employers must offer higher wages to attract workers to it; office work, on the other hand, is sought after for its comfort and social status, so many people accept lower pay just to get it.**

### Conseil
Sur une question d'opinion, appuie toujours ta réponse sur un élément du texte (ici, la phrase sur le sacrifice consenti pour devenir “white collar worker”) plutôt que de donner un avis complètement déconnecté du passage : cela montre au correcteur que l'opinion reste ancrée dans la compréhension du document.
